We prove this by induction on~$m$. If $m = 0$, the claim is that
$\Th{Q} \Proves \eq[(
um{n} + \Obj 0)][
um{n}]$. This follows by
axiom~$!Q_4$.  Now suppose the claim for $m$; let's prove the claim
for $m+1$, i.e., prove that $\Th{Q} \Proves \eq[(
um{n} +
  
um{m+1})][
um{n+m+1}]$. Note that $
um{m+1}$ is just $
um{m}'$,
and $
um{n+m+1}$ is just $
um{n+m}'$.  By axiom $!Q_5$, $\Th{Q}
\Proves \eq[(
um{n} + 
um{m}')][(
um{n}+
um{m})']$. By induction
hypothesis, $\Th{Q} \Proves \eq[(
um{n} + 
um{m})][
um{n+m}]$. So
$\Th{Q} \Proves \eq[(
um{n} + 
um{m}')][
um{n+m}']$.
